patterns.text: Bare for about 181 days each farming year, from 24 Oct to 22 Apr.
Cotton at mid-season faced heat in 10 of the last 10 seasons.
Main-season rainfall is falling since 1991, a statistically clear trend in NASA POWER data (7.0 mm per decade).
Water stored on land in this region (~300 km) has fallen about 2.11 cm per year since 2002 (GRACE/GRACE-FO).

evidence.name: Continuous cotton
evidence.verdict: This is your current rotation. Every other option is compared with it.
assumptions_L: A soil arrow needs a difference of at least 2 points in a season. An arrow changes when the option wins or loses in at least 16 of 24 seasons.
Bare soil uses a crop coefficient of 0.25 after at least 5 mm of rain or irrigation in 3 days, and 0.10 otherwise.
A crop is heat-hit after 3 hot days in its flowering window. The frost threshold, when applied, is 2 °C.
The heavy-rain index uses rain events of at least 12.7 mm. Local slope is omitted.
The soil score averages six indicators of field practices. Newly reached soil is assumed to start at field capacity.
The residue model uses the time between crops. Residue machinery multiplies predicted burning pressure by 0.3.
The water arrow compares water use by crops and soil, with a 3% threshold in each season. Irrigation pumping is shown alongside it.
For crops outside ponded rice, the model assumes 60% of pumped water reaches the crop roots and tests 50% to 75%.
Crop stages use global fractions applied to the length of the local calendar.
For rainfed crops, the water arrow compares the fraction of mid-season days with strong dry stress, using a 0.05 difference to count a win.
0.30 m for rice, 0.15 m for all others. Starting root depths follow the corresponding Punjab rice and non-rice defaults where sections 7.3 and 7.5 only specify mature roots.
0.55. The specification gives a bare-soil evaporation layer but no available-water threshold for that layer.

why: This rotation is the baseline for the season-by-season comparison.
evidence: Replayed through 24 real seasons (2001 to 2024) of NASA POWER weather.
Median soil score 51.3 (range 44.3 to 55.7) vs 51.3 now. Water used by crops and soil 1335 mm/yr vs 1335 mm/yr.
benefits: Deep roots can break up compacted layers and reach water further down.
gaps: Disease and nutrient balance are not modelled.
Crop dates are regional defaults from GGCMI. Check them for your field.
Income is not modelled. Check local prices.
risks: Cotton faced heat at flowering in 24 of 24 seasons.
Check this with your local agriculture office or extension service (for example a Krishi Vigyan Kendra in India) before changing your rotation.

why: Your field is usually bare for about 183 days from 10-28 to 04-18. Hairy vetch fits that window in 100% of the last 24 seasons.
evidence: Replayed through 24 real seasons (2001 to 2024) of NASA POWER weather.
Median soil score 86.5 (range 82.2 to 89.0) vs 51.3 now. Water used by crops and soil 1444 mm/yr vs 1335 mm/yr.
benefits: Deep roots can break up compacted layers and reach water further down.
Legumes host bacteria that pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, so the next crop may need less fertiliser.
Living roots and leaves protect bare soil from sun, wind and heavy rain, and feed soil life.
The score for days with living roots rose from 0.50 to 0.83.
The score for time with nitrogen-fixing crops rose from 0.00 to 0.98.
The score for crop families rotated (breaks pest and disease cycles) rose from 0.00 to 0.60.
The score for heavy rain landing on bare soil rose from 0.58 to 0.78.
gaps: Disease and nutrient balance are not modelled.
Crop dates are regional defaults from GGCMI. Check them for your field.
Income is not modelled. Check local prices.
risks: Cotton faced heat at flowering in 24 of 24 seasons.
Check seed availability and the time needed to prepare the field between crops.
Check this with your local agriculture office or extension service (for example a Krishi Vigyan Kendra in India) before changing your rotation.
